## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The pull-request description needs a `## Testing` section, because without one it breaks a project policy rule. Separately, `slugify` drops accented and non-Latin letters. Titles like "Café" lose characters, and fully non-Latin titles collapse to an empty slug. No critical defects were found in the two changed files.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- PR body — correctness — The pull-request description has no `## Testing` section, which breaks the project rule in AGENTS.md:4: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." The body has only one paragraph, which describes what `slugify` does and says nothing about how the change was checked. To fix this, add a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified, for example by running `tests/test_slug.py`. — The pull request does not meet a stated contributor rule, and maintainers have no record of how the change was verified.
- app/slug.py:13 — correctness — A title with accented or non-Latin letters loses those letters: `slugify("Café Menu")` returns `"caf-menu"`, and `slugify("日本語")` returns `""`. The pattern `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every character outside ASCII lowercase letters and digits as a separator. The PR body promises to replace "non-alphanumeric characters", but Python considers `é` and `日` alphanumeric. One fix is to normalize with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` and drop combining marks before the substitution, then decide what to do with titles that still produce an empty slug (for example, reject them or fall back to an ID). Add test cases for both kinds of input. — Pages with accented titles get wrong URLs. Any titles made only of non-Latin characters all get the same empty slug, so their URLs collide or become invalid.

## Suggestions
(none)

## Strengths
- `tests/test_slug.py` covers the boundary cases at both ends: repeated separators with surrounding whitespace, input made only of separators (`"---"`), and the empty string.
- Both new modules start with a docstring that describes their purpose, as AGENTS.md:3 requires.
